method: Automated inventory read every source, evidence, pathway, profile and review record in the exact manifest candidate for this ISO.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.123 (printed p.123), paragraphs 270–271, water stress and drought vulnerability.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2021-07 reports: The diagnostic identifies the central area, Walvis Bay–Swakopmund coast and Cuvelai as highly water-stressed; northern regions have the largest shares lacking safe water and sanitation.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.124 (printed p.124), paragraphs 271–274, rainfall, rural livelihoods and water-related child outcomes.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2021-07 reports: The report links recurring drought and volatile rainfall with poverty risks for rural households reliant on agriculture; water and sanitation shortfalls are associated with child stunting.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.99 (printed p.99), paragraph 193 and Figure 32, regional poverty profile based on 2015/16 data.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2021-07 reports: The report’s 2015/16 profile places poverty above the national average in Kavango East, Kunene, Omaheke and Zambezi; poor groups included children, older people and female-headed households.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.11 (printed p.10), 2021/22 rainfall-season performance.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023-01 reports: In 2021/22, delayed rains and prolonged dry spells left crop areas with below-average harvests, including northern Kunene and Omusati and parts of Oshana and Otjozondjupa.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.11 (printed p.10), vulnerability context, drought.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023-01 reports: NAMVAC reported ongoing drought effects in Kunene, Erongo and Omusati; Kunene had eight consecutive drought years, with livestock deaths, lost income and depleted grazing and water.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.20 (printed p.15), household dietary diversity score by region.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023-01 reports: In 2022, households consuming only zero to two food groups were most prevalent in Kunene (42%), Kavango East (39.7%), Oshikoto (30.4%) and Kavango West (29.7%).
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.5 (printed p.5), Overview, regional drought exposure and rural livelihoods.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2022 reports: IFRC names Kunene, Erongo, Omusati and Omaheke as drought-prone; communal crop/livestock households were heavily affected.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.5 (printed p.5), 2018/19 drought and competition for water/grazing.

evidence.compact_statement: The 2022 IFRC report describes human–wildlife conflict over water and grazing during the 2018/19 drought. This is a livelihood and protection interaction, not evidence of interpersonal or armed conflict.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.11 (printed p.11), assessment findings on drought-induced migration and resource competition.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2022 reports: Below-average rainfall prompted pastoral migration for water/grazing within and across Namibia–Angola; IFRC says migration heightened resource competition and conflict.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2022 reports: Women spent longer fetching water; children sometimes left school as pastoral households moved, and many such households were female-headed.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.6 (printed p.6), actions following the 2019 drought declaration.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2022 reports: Red Cross actions included Kunene borehole repairs, solar pumps, WASH outreach and cash aid in 2019–21.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.20 (printed section p.6), smallholder credit constraints and communal land tenure.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023 reports: Smallholders had limited credit; missing collateral linked to communal-land titling, low productivity and recurrent climate shocks constrained investment, while AgriBank outreach to communal farmers was limited.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.43 (printed p.29), livestock insurance and financial risk-transfer market.

geographies: communal areas north of the Veterinary Cordon Fence
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023 reports: The 2023 diagnostic found agricultural insurance largely limited to commercial farmers; proposed or tested drought-index products included options for communal farmers in Kavango East, Kavango West and Zambezi.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.27 (printed p.13), existing National Disaster Fund and proposed National Drought Fund.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023 reports: The National Disaster Fund was active but its broad mandate was assessed as inefficient for disaster finance; a separate National Drought Fund remained a proposal in a pending policy.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.4, Executive Summary, 2024/25 drought impacts and IPC assessment.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2026-06 reports: Review reports 1.4 million assessed people in IPC Phase 3+ during the 2024/25 drought, associated with low rainfall, crop failure, livestock losses and higher food prices.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.4, Executive Summary, scale and timing of response.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2026-06 reports: Response reached about 385,000 households across all 14 regions, but warnings did not trigger timely action and aid often arrived after livelihoods eroded.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.23 (printed p.24), water-response coordination, decentralization and preparedness gaps.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2026-06 reports: Regional committees were often not functional or empowered; centralized funds and authority constrained local action, while contingency plans were weak or not operationalized.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical pp.22–23 (printed pp.23–24), water-response performance and protection risks.

evidence.compact_statement: The June 2026 after-action review reports that water trucking maintained basic access for households and livestock and reduced unsafe coping, especially for women, while finding the response under-scaled for long-term resilience. This is a retrospective review finding, not a quantified causal evaluation.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.32 (printed p.33), gender and protection findings.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2026-06 reports: Some targeting included female-headed households and pregnant women, but review found no comprehensive gender analysis and identified exclusion and safety risks at distribution sites.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

pathways.compact_statement: The 2022 IFRC assessment associates drought-related pastoral movement with resource competition and unspecified conflict, not an armed-conflict forecast.
alternative_explanations: Land access, service provision, pre-existing resource arrangements and livelihood conditions also shape competition; mobility is an established risk-management practice.
pathways.uncertainty: Localized qualitative assessment. Conflict is unspecified and must not be read as armed violence, ethnic hostility or a general risk posed by migrants.
recommendations: No structural linkage issue identified; review each cited passage for its specific causal link, alternatives and uncertainty before treating the pathway as verified.
